name: VoxApp API
description:
The VoxApp Integration API lets you trigger calls and messages, manage contacts, fetch call results, and subscribe to webhook events from your own systems.

All endpoints below live under `/api/v1` and are designed for server-to-server integration — they are what platforms like Zapier, Make, n8n, and custom backends use to drive VoxApp.

## Getting started

1. Create an OAuth2 client in your VoxApp dashboard at [my.voxapp.com](https://my.voxapp.com/) under **Settings → Developers**.
2. Use the **authorization code** flow if you're building a user-facing integration (Zapier-style), or **client credentials** if it's a backend-only integration.
3. Include the access token on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `calls:read` | View call history and details |
| `calls:write` | Trigger outbound and web calls, send SMS, create meetings |
| `contacts:read` | View contacts |
| `contacts:write` | Create and update contacts, send emails |
| `assistants:read` | View assistants |
| `webhooks:manage` | Create and manage webhook subscriptions |

Default scopes if none requested: `calls:read`, `contacts:read`, `assistants:read`.

## Rate limits

Most endpoints are rate-limited per-token. Limits are returned in standard `X-RateLimit-*` headers. If you exceed your limit you'll get an HTTP 429.

## Errors

Errors are returned as JSON with an `error` or `message` key plus the standard HTTP status code. Validation failures return `422` with a `errors` object keyed by field name.
